newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian C. Bank rate cut pushes T-bill yields down.
newsitem.headline: Russian C. Bank rate cut pushes T-bill yields down.

text.p: Yields on long-term GKO discount Treasury bills fell to record lows in active trading on Friday after the Central Bank announced a cut in its refinancing rate, dealers said.
One year T-bill yields fell to 19.0 percent from 20.5-21.0 percent at the opening.

"On long-term T-bills the market opened with the yields of 20.5-21.0 percent and stabilised at this level, but after the news about the refinancing rate cuts everyone rushed to buy long-term paper," a Bank Menatep dealer said.
"And this was despite the fact that there was less money in the trading system than on Wednesday."
Banks had transferred 1.89 trillion roubles to the system for Friday's trading. By 0818 turnover had reached 3.16 trillion roubles.
Russian markets were closed on Thursday for the Independence Day holiday.
The Central Bank said on Friday it will cut its refinancing rate from June 16 to 24 percent from 36 percent. It also cut rates on Lombard loans.
At 0830 GMT the 25001 bills, maturing on June 6, 1999, were the day's strongest gainer, rising 1.80 to 102.99. The price rise on one year T-bills was between 0.8-1.0.
Dealers said Russian investors were behind the buying, and were seeking paper for their clients'.
They said the price rise could cool down by the end of trading and forecast prices would end off highs as banks have to free a lot of funds for next Wednesday's auctions.
The Finance Ministry will offer a total of 20 trillion roubles of T-bills and OFZ interest-bearing bonds for auctions on Wendesday.
Overnight rates fell to 15-16 percent annual from 25-30 percent on Wednesday night.
Interbank roubles for today delivery were 5,759-5,761 per dollar after 5,763-5,765 for tomorrow delivery late Wednesday.
